direction: Rule-structured synthetic knowledge graph, transductive versus inductive. Generate a family-tree knowledge graph (500 people, relations parent / sibling / grandparent / uncle derived by rules). Train TransE and a small path-based model (2-hop relational message passing) and test on held-out triples of the same graph and on a freshly generated graph with new entities; report MRR in both settings. Keep it a small CPU study with reimplemented baselines, at least 5 seeds where cheap, and report negative or mixed results plainly.

notes.note: TransE, TransE+fold-in, oracle, tuned on val

decisions.decision: Uncle relation is gender-neutral (sibling of a parent: uncle or aunt) so that every relation is exactly rule-derivable from parent facts without a gender attribute; sibling = full sibling (shared both parents); sibling pairs are split as one unit so the mirror triple cannot leak.

Inductive world = second independently generated 500-person graph; its triples are split 80/10/10 like graph 1; observed message graph = its train+val units, test = its held-out 10%. Ties in ranks are split evenly (realistic rank). Filtered ranking uses all true triples of the graph.

TransE tuned on validation split of separate graph seeds 100,101 over three rounds (margin, norm, dim, epochs; best margin 8, L1, dim 64, 200 epochs, interior optimum). Path-MP tuned over epochs {3,6} x lr {0.003,0.01}: tie at 3 vs 6 epochs, chose 3 (cheaper), lr 0.003. A fold-in variant of TransE (new entity vectors fitted with relations frozen) and a hand-written rule oracle added as stronger / reference baselines.
